evidence.quoted_text:
base.mkdir(mode=0o700, parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        require(not base.stat().st_mode & 0o077,
                "private record directory must have mode 0700: " + str(base))
        name = ("run-" + time.strftime("%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ", time.gmtime())
                + "-" + uuid.uuid4().hex[:6])
        self.run_dir = base / name
        self.run_dir.mkdir(mode=0o700)
evidence.reason: The shown claim path creates the record base and the new run directory but never fsyncs the base directory entry. The later `durable_write` on the receipt only makes the receipt and its containing run directory durable; it does not persist the run-directory entry in `base`. If power is lost after admission is claimed, the recovery state (prior SHA and trigger state) can disappear while the host remains held. This is a real crash-consistency defect in the intended durable recovery path, not merely a new hardening requirement. The minimal fix is to fsync `base` after creating the run directory, fsync `base`'s parent when the invocation created `base`, and fail closed if either sync fails.
